key_insight: Greedy decoding in LLMs is not fully deterministic across numerical precision: the same prompt and model can diverge between BF16 and FP16 because tiny logit-margin differences can flip the chosen token and cascade downstream.
engineering_relevance: Inference stacks that assume precision-invariant greedy decoding may need selective higher-precision recomputation at the LM head to improve output stability with minimal latency overhead in low-batch serving.
method: Compared BF16 vs FP16 greedy decoding on six models across three benchmarks, plus a 12B case, to measure exact output divergence.
Analyzed error propagation and found divergence is driven mainly by the top-two logit margin relative to perturbation between candidate tokens, not by accumulated body error alone.
Tested selective FP32 LM-head recomputation when the margin falls below a threshold as a low-overhead mitigation.
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated models and benchmarks, 49–100% of prompts diverged across precision, and selective FP32 LM-head recomputation improved exact agreement by 22–36 percentage points on A10G with under 4% latency overhead in low-batch single-stream inference.
watch_item: The mitigation is not universal: its benefit drops when body-originated error dominates, especially at batch size ≥8 and under end-to-end FP8.
paper_title: Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant: Cross-Precision Output Divergence in LLM Inference
